items.title: Israel says Khamenei killed in joint US-Israeli strikes on Iran

featured_image.name: US and Isreal launch a major attack on Iran

items.description:
Iranian Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei was killed Saturday in a massive joint U.S.-Israeli military operation targeting Tehran and cities across Iran, according to multiple Israeli officials. A senior Israeli official told Reuters that Khamenei's body had been found in the ruins of his compound. Israeli Ambassador to Washington Yechiel Leiter confirmed the killing to U.S. officials, according to Axios reporter Barak Ravid.[1][2][3]

The 86-year-old Khamenei, who had led the Islamic Republic since 1989, was struck in the opening salvo of the operation as Israeli and American forces simultaneously hit three separate gatherings of senior Iranian officials, an Israeli military official told reporters. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and President Donald Trump were both shown an image of Khamenei's body recovered from his compound, Israel's Channel 12 reported.[4][5][1]

items.title: FBI on high alert as U.S., Israel strike Iran

featured_image.name: Iran Strikes: Kash Patel Puts FBI Counterterrorism Teams on ...

items.description:
FBI Director Kash Patel placed the bureau's counterterrorism and counterintelligence teams on high alert Saturday after the United States and Israel launched coordinated military strikes on Iran in what the Pentagon has dubbed "Operation Epic Fury."

"FBI personnel are fully engaged on the situation overseas. Last night I instructed our Counterterrorism and intelligence teams to be on high alert and mobilize all assisting security assets needed," Patel wrote on X. "Our JTTFs throughout the country are working 24/7, as always, to address and disrupt any potential threats to the homeland."[1]

The directive came as U.S. Central Command confirmed that strikes began at 1:15 a.m. ET on February 28, targeting Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps command facilities, air defense systems, missile launch sites, and military airfields across Iran.[2]

items.title: Gulf states condemn Iran after strikes hit US bases across region

featured_image.name: US, Israel bomb Iran: A timeline of talks and threats leading up to ...

items.description: World leaders scrambled to respond on Saturday as the United States and Israel launched joint military strikes on Iran, with governments from Moscow to Riyadh warning the offensive risks plunging the Middle East into a wider, uncontrollable conflict. The strikes, codenamed Operation Epic Fury by the Pentagon, prompted retaliatory Iranian missile attacks on U.S. military bases across the Persian Gulf, hitting targets in Bahrain, Kuwait, the United Arab Emirates, Qatar, and Jordan — drawing a wave of condemnation and alarm from capitals worldwide.[1][2][3]

items.title: Israel locks down as Iran fires retaliatory missiles

featured_image.name: Iran says missiles fired at Israel in response to assassinations

items.description:
Air raid sirens blared across Israel on Saturday as Iranian ballistic missiles streaked toward the country in retaliation for a joint U.S.-Israeli military operation against Iran, sending millions of civilians rushing to bomb shelters and fortified rooms in what became a nationwide lockdown.

Defense Minister Israel Katz declared a state of emergency across the country, warning the public of incoming Iranian missile and drone attacks. The Israel Defense Forces ordered all civilians to remain in protected spaces until further notice, stating that its air defense array was "detecting and intercepting threats". Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps said it had launched a "first wave of large-scale missile and drone attacks" toward Israel in response to the strikes.[1][2][3]

items.title: Iran's defense chief, IRGC commander killed in US-Israeli strikes

featured_image.name: Iranian Revolutionary Guard leader may have been killed in airstrikes as several IRGC and civilian decision-makers reported dead in decapitation airstrikes

items.description: Iranian Defense Minister Amir Nasirzadeh and Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps commander Gen. Mohammad Pakpour were killed in coordinated US-Israeli strikes on Iran Saturday morning, according to three sources cited by Reuters. The deaths represent the highest-profile casualties since the joint military operation — dubbed "Epic Fury" by the United States and "Lion's Roar" by Israel — began early Saturday with strikes across Tehran and other Iranian cities.[1][2][3]

items.title: Saudi, UAE leaders unite against Iran after missiles rock Gulf capitals

featured_image.name: KUNA : Mohammad bin Zayed, Mohammad bin Salman meet on ...

items.description:
Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman called UAE President Sheikh Mohammed bin Zayed Al Nahyan on Saturday to condemn Iranian missile strikes that rocked Gulf capitals from Abu Dhabi to Doha, in a show of solidarity that bridges a months-long rift between the two Gulf powers over Yemen.

During the call, the Saudi crown prince expressed the Kingdom's "full solidarity" with the UAE and pledged readiness to "place all its capabilities" at Abu Dhabi's disposal, according to the UAE's official news agency WAM. Sheikh Mohammed bin Zayed expressed appreciation for Saudi Arabia's "firm stance" and "fraternal solidarity," and both leaders warned that the Iranian strikes constituted "a dangerous escalation that threatens regional security and undermines stability". They called for restraint and diplomatic solutions to preserve regional security.[1][2]

items.title: UN Security Council holds emergency session on US-Israel strikes against Iran

featured_image.name: UN urges restraint as Iran and Israel trade barbs at Security Council

items.description:
The United Nations Security Council is set to convene an emergency session at 4 p.m. EST Saturday after the United States and Israel launched coordinated military strikes against Iran earlier in the day, plunging the Middle East into a new armed conflict. Iran has retaliated with missile and drone attacks targeting Israeli and U.S. military installations across the region, including in Jordan, Syria, Kuwait, Bahrain, Qatar, Saudi Arabia, and the United Arab Emirates.

The emergency meeting was requested by France, Russia, China, Bahrain, and Colombia, according to Reuters. Russia's UN mission said it called the session "in response to the unprovoked act of military aggression by the United States and Israel against the Islamic Republic of Iran," while pledging to urge Washington and Jerusalem "to immediately halt their unlawful and provocative actions," according to U.S. News.[1][2]

items.title: Iran launches retaliatory strikes on US bases after joint US-Israeli assault

featured_image.name: Iran live updates: U.S. and Israel launch strikes, Trump dubs attack 'Operation Epic Fury'

items.description: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi told the United Nations on Saturday that all American and Israeli military bases, facilities, and assets across the Middle East would be considered legitimate targets, as Iran launched retaliatory missile strikes against US installations in multiple Gulf states following a joint US-Israeli military assault on Iranian territory.

items.title: Russia condemns US-Israeli strikes on Iran, evacuates citizens

featured_image.name: Russia condemns US and Israel's attack on Iran

items.description:
Russia's Foreign Ministry on Saturday sharply condemned the joint U.S.-Israeli military strikes on Iran, calling them "a pre-planned and unprovoked act of armed aggression against a sovereign and independent U.N. member state" and warning the attacks risk plunging the Middle East into chaos.[1][2]

In a statement posted to Telegram, the ministry accused Washington and Tel Aviv of "hiding behind" concerns about Iran's nuclear program while pursuing regime change. It warned the strikes could trigger a "humanitarian, economic and possibly radiological catastrophe" in the region, accusing the United States and Israel of "plunging the Middle East into an abyss of uncontrolled escalation".[3][2]

items.title: Israel claims top Iranian commanders killed in strikes

featured_image.name: US, Israel launch strikes on Iran. See photos

items.description: Israeli media reported Saturday that several high-ranking Iranian officials were killed in the coordinated US-Israel military strikes on Iran, in what analysts are describing as an apparent decapitation operation targeting the Islamic Republic's top leadership. The claims, which remain disputed by Tehran, came as explosions rocked cities across Iran on February 28, 2026.

items.title: Pakistan rules out talks with Afghanistan as fighting enters third day

featured_image.name: Afghanistan says Pakistan fighter jet down as cross-border ...

items.description:
Pakistan and Afghanistan continued to exchange fire along their contested border on Saturday, with Islamabad ruling out negotiations and demanding Kabul end its alleged support for militant groups, as the most serious military confrontation between the two neighbors in years showed no signs of abating.

Pakistan's prime minister's spokesperson told Pakistani television on Saturday that "there won't be talks" and "there's no negotiation," insisting Afghanistan must first cease harboring militants. The statement came despite the Taliban government expressing willingness to resolve the crisis through dialogue. The European Union's foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas also urged both nations Saturday to lower tensions, warning the violence could destabilize the wider region.[1]

items.title: CIA assessed IRGC hardliners would replace Khamenei if killed in U.S.-Israeli strikes

featured_image.name: Exclusive: Prior to Iran attacks, CIA assessed Khamenei ...

items.description:
In the lead-up to Saturday's joint U.S. and Israeli military operation against Iran, the Central Intelligence Agency assessed that even if Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei were killed, he would most likely be succeeded by hardline figures from the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps rather than reformist elements, according to a Reuters report citing two sources briefed on the intelligence.[1]

The finding underscores a tension at the heart of President Trump's stated ambition to topple Iran's clerical establishment: the intelligence community's own analysis suggests military force alone may not produce the kind of political transformation Washington seeks.

items.title: Oil majors halt Strait of Hormuz shipments amid US-Iran strikes

featured_image.name: Oil: Iran partially closes Strait of Hormuz amid U.S. nuclear talks

items.description:
Maritime traffic through the Strait of Hormuz ground to a near-halt on Saturday as oil majors and trading houses suspended crude oil, fuel, and liquefied natural gas shipments following joint US-Israeli military strikes on Iran. Tracking data showed tanker speeds dropping to near zero as shipowners pulled vessels from the waterway that carries roughly 20 percent of the world's seaborne oil trade.[1][2]

Several major oil companies and leading trading firms halted shipments through the strait as Iran declared the waterway closed to navigation, according to Reuters, citing four trading sources. "Our vessels will remain stationary for a number of days," a senior executive at a prominent trading firm said. The US Navy warned against navigating in the operational zone, which encompasses the entirety of the Gulf, the Gulf of Oman, the Arabian Sea, and the Strait of Hormuz, saying it could not guarantee the safety of commercial vessels.[2]

items.title: Trump announces 'major combat operations' in Iran

featured_image.name: Trump 'not thrilled' with Iran but undecided on attack

items.description:
President Donald Trump told reporters on Friday that he was "not happy" with the state of nuclear negotiations with Iran and warned that "sometimes you have to" use military force, remarks that proved to be a prelude to the launch of U.S. combat operations against Iran early Saturday.

Speaking outside the White House before departing for Texas, Trump said he had not yet made a final decision on strikes but expressed deep frustration with Tehran's negotiating posture. "I'm not happy with the fact that they're not willing to give us what we have to have," he said, according to Politico. "We're not thrilled with the way they're negotiating."[1][2]

Hours later, Trump announced on Truth Social that the United States had begun "major combat operations" in Iran, according to Reuters.[3]

items.title: Houthis to resume Red Sea attacks after U.S.-Israeli strikes on Iran

featured_image.name: Houthi threaten to resume Red Sea attacks on shipping

items.description:
Yemen's Iran-backed Houthi rebels have decided to resume missile and drone attacks on Red Sea shipping routes and Israel in response to the joint U.S.-Israeli military strikes on Iran launched on February 28, two senior Houthi officials told the Associated Press. One official said the first attack could come as soon as "tonight," though no formal announcement had been issued by the Houthi leadership.[1][2][3]

The decision marks the collapse of a ceasefire between the Houthis and the United States that had been in place since May 2025, when the Trump administration and the group struck an Oman-brokered deal to halt mutual hostilities. Under that agreement, the Houthis ceased attacks on commercial shipping in the Red Sea and the Bab al-Mandab Strait, while the U.S. ended its bombing campaign in Yemen. The Houthis had also stopped targeting Israel following an October 2025 ceasefire that reduced fighting in Gaza.[4][5][6][1]

items.title: Iran fires ballistic missiles at UAE in first direct attack

featured_image.name: Iran fires ballistic missiles at U.S. Al Dhafra Air Base in ...

items.description: The United Arab Emirates said on Saturday that its air defense systems intercepted multiple Iranian ballistic missiles targeting the country, though falling debris killed one civilian in Abu Dhabi and caused material damage in a residential area. The attack came as Iran launched retaliatory strikes across the Gulf following a joint U.S.-Israeli military operation against targets inside Iran.[1][2][3][4]

items.title: Russia may halt peace talks unless Ukraine cedes territory

featured_image.name: Russia and Ukraine stick to their demands ahead of planned ...

items.description:
Russian officials increasingly see little reason to continue U.S.-led peace negotiations with Ukraine unless Kyiv signals a willingness to give up territory as part of a settlement, Bloomberg News reported Saturday, raising the prospect of a collapse in diplomacy as the war enters its fifth year.[1][2]

Talks scheduled for next week will be decisive in whether the sides can move toward an agreement to end the conflict, two people close to the Kremlin told Bloomberg. Russia will likely walk away if Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy fails to make the concession, the people said. Reuters confirmed the report but said it could not independently verify the claims.[3][1]

items.title: Ohio State researchers turn moon dust into durable structures via 3D laser printing

featured_image.name: 3D-printed lunar base may be on the way

items.description:
Researchers at Ohio State University have demonstrated that laser-based 3D printing can transform simulated lunar soil into strong, heat-resistant structures, a advance that could one day allow astronauts to build habitats on the Moon using materials already found on its surface.

The study, published in the journal Acta Astronautica, offers a proof of concept for a technique that would eliminate the need to haul construction materials from Earth — a prospect that currently costs an estimated $1 million or more per kilogram, according to the researchers.[1]

items.title: Czech scientists detect lightning on Mars from orbit for the first time

featured_image.name: Listen to the crackle of Martian 'mini-lightning'

items.description: A team of Czech scientists has identified a lightning-generated radio signal in data from NASA's MAVEN spacecraft, providing the first orbital evidence of electrical discharge activity in the Martian atmosphere. The finding, published February 27 in the journal Science Advances, adds a new dimension to the growing body of evidence that Mars is an electrically active world.[1][2]

items.title: Trump launched Iran strikes despite intel doubting his missile threat claims

featured_image.name: President Trump addresses the nation after US strikes nuclear sites in Iran

items.description: Just days before the United States launched what President Donald Trump called "major combat operations" in Iran on Saturday, intelligence sources and weapons experts were pushing back on one of the administration's central justifications for military action: that Iran was close to building missiles capable of striking the American homeland.
